models.name: Claude Opus 5
strengths: Tops Anthropic's Frontier-Bench v0.1 agentic-coding run at 43.3% — above Claude Fable 5 (33.7%) and more than double Opus 4.8 (18.7%), at a lower cost per task
Fable-class coding at half Fable's price ($5/$25 vs $10/$50) — on CursorBench 3.2 at max effort it lands within 0.5% of Fable 5's peak score at about half the cost per task
Five-rung effort dial (low → max) so you can trade cost against capability per request; low/medium are unusually strong on this model
1M-token context as both default and maximum, 128K max output, and a 512-token prompt-cache minimum (half Opus 4.8's)
weaknesses: Per-benchmark public numbers are thin — released 2026-07-23, so SWE-bench Verified, GPQA and the rest aren't published or third-party-verified yet; the coding score is agentic-suite-led, not SWE-bench-anchored
The headline Frontier-Bench comparison is Anthropic's own internal run on its own harness — directional for cross-lab ranking, not settled
Still Opus-priced: $5/$25 is far above Sonnet 5 or the open tiers for bulk work
Thinking is now on by default, and disabling it is only allowed at 'high' effort or below — quiet cost and behaviour change if you're porting Opus 4.8 code across
models.verdict: The new default for hard coding and agent work: it matches or beats Fable 5 on the agentic suites its own lab publishes, at half the price — just treat the benchmark picture as early until third parties verify it.
models.coding_basis: Frontier-Bench v0.1 43.3% (#1, ahead of Fable 5's 33.7%) and CursorBench 3.2 within 0.5% of Fable 5's peak at max effort — calibrated against Fable 5 (95). SWE-bench Verified not yet published, so this is an agentic-suite-led estimate, not a SWE-bench number.
use_well: Start at 'xhigh' effort for coding and agentic work, 'high' elsewhere — then sweep down. Low and medium punch well above their weight here, and effort is the main cost lever.
Give it the whole task spec in one first message and let it run — it's built for long autonomous sessions, and drip-feeding the task across turns costs more and works less well.
Thinking is ON by default now (it wasn't on Opus 4.8) — so re-check your max_tokens, or responses can truncate mid-answer.
It verifies its own work without being asked. Delete any 'double-check your answer' instructions you carried over — they now cause redundant work.

models.name: Kimi K3
strengths: Front-end champion — #1 in the Frontend Code Arena (1679 Elo), ahead of Claude Fable 5, winning 6 of 7 frontend categories in blind dev testing
2.8T-param MoE (~16 of 896 experts active per token) — the largest open-weight model to date; 1M-token context with native vision
Cheap for its tier at $3/$15 per M, with ~$0.30/M cache-hit input (90%+ cache-hit rates typical in coding loops)
weaknesses: Its headline win is frontend/web-dev coding; broad benchmarks (SWE-bench Verified, GPQA) not yet published, so overall coding is a frontend-led estimate
Open weights not released until ~2026-07-27 — 'open-weight' isn't yet self-hostable
Output at $15/M is well above the cheap open tiers (DeepSeek/Qwen) for bulk work
models.verdict: Reach for it for frontend and web-dev coding, where it tops the arena ahead of even Fable 5 at a fraction of the price — but treat its broader coding strength as unproven until SWE-bench lands.
models.coding_basis: Frontend Code Arena #1 (1679 Elo), ahead of Fable 5, winning 6 of 7 frontend categories; general SWE-bench Verified not yet published — score is frontend-led.
use_well: Reach for it on frontend and web-UI builds — that's where it tops the arena; treat broader coding as unproven until SWE-bench lands.
Coding loops hit ~$0.30/M cache-hit input — keep one long session going instead of restarting, and the real cost drops well below sticker.
Open weights aren't due until ~July 27 — don't plan a self-host around it yet.

models.name: Claude Fable 5
strengths: Highest SWE-bench Verified on the board (~95.5% self-announced, ~95% independent)
Anthropic's most capable widely-available model; built for long-horizon autonomous agents
1M-token context at standard pricing
Always-on thinking; high-resolution vision
weaknesses: Most expensive model here: $10/$50 per M — exactly 2x Opus 4.8
Reported availability/export restrictions (was briefly pulled offline June 2026)

Overkill and overpriced for routine work

Thinking is always on — give it the complete task up front in one well-specified message and let it run; drip-feeding steps wastes its strength.

benchmarks_legend.swe_bench: SWE-bench Verified — % of real-world GitHub issues resolved end-to-end (agentic coding). Note: several 2026 models published only SWE-bench Pro, a different/harder variant, so their Verified cell is null.
benchmarks_legend.gpqa: GPQA Diamond — % correct on graduate-level, Google-proof science reasoning questions.
benchmarks_legend.aime: AIME — % on advanced high-school competition math (American Invitational Mathematics Examination).
benchmarks_legend.mmlu_pro: MMLU-Pro — % on a harder, multi-discipline knowledge and reasoning benchmark.
benchmarks_legend.lmarena_elo: LMArena text Elo — human head-to-head preference rating (higher = preferred more often).

notes: Data snapshot 2026-07-24. Claude Opus 5 (released 2026-07-23) is added at Anthropic's published $5/$25 pricing, which multiple outlets corroborate as half Fable 5's rate; its per-benchmark numbers (SWE-bench Verified, GPQA) are not published or third-party-verified yet, so those cells are blank and its coding score is an agentic-suite-led estimate at medium confidence. Data snapshot 2026-07-24 (all vendor list prices re-verified 2026-07-24; the 2026-07-20 auto-check's six OpenRouter price flags were all confirmed to be provider pass-through, not list-price changes). Kimi K3 (released 2026-07-16) is scored on its frontend-coding lead — #1 in the Frontend Code Arena ahead of Fable 5; its $3/$15 pricing and 1M context are sourced, but SWE-bench Verified is not yet published and open weights are due ~2026-07-27, so it carries medium overall confidence. Pricing is verified against official vendor pricing pages (standard tier, USD per 1M tokens) — treat it as the reliable layer. Benchmarks are directional: most come from third-party aggregators (Artificial Analysis, Vellum, llm-stats, vals.ai), not primary vendor cards, and several 2026 models publish only agentic evals (SWE-bench Pro, Terminal-Bench) that don't map to SWE-bench Verified — those cells are left blank rather than cross-filed. A blank (—) means 'not reliably sourced,' never a guess. Note: Sonnet 5 shows its current intro price ($2/$10; rises to $3/$15 on Sept 1, 2026). Re-verify any single benchmark against a primary leaderboard before betting real spend on it.

usage.basis: No single "most used" exists — each lens measures a different population and ranks models differently. Figures are ~June–July 2026 and lag a couple of weeks, so the newest models (GPT-5.6, Grok 4.5, Sonnet 5) aren't ranked yet.

lenses.label: Developers
lenses.note: Cheap open-weight models win on raw volume; Anthropic & OpenAI win on dollars spent. Chinese labs are ~44–52% of all tokens.

lenses.label: Preference
lenses.note: A quality-preference signal, not usage. ~7.3M votes; the whole top tier sits within ~55 Elo — the tightest ever.

lenses.label: Consumers
lenses.note: Consumer web visits only (undercounts mobile & embedded) — a totally different crowd from the API developers.

coding_score_note: Coding score (0–100) is a unified, comparable coding-ability estimate. Where an official SWE-bench Verified % exists it IS that number (high confidence). Where it doesn't — several strong 2026 models ship before formal benchmarks — it's estimated from sourced signals (Artificial Analysis Coding Index, LMArena Code Elo, SWE-bench Pro, LiveCodeBench) calibrated against the benchmarked models (medium confidence), or expert consensus (low). Each row shows its basis and confidence. These signals sometimes disagree — treat medium/low scores as directional.
use_well_note: use_well = practical, plain-English guidance on getting the most from a model you already have. Derived from the model's sourced pricing, context, cache and mode facts above (plus vendor-documented features like Claude's adaptive thinking) — guidance, not benchmarks. Same independence rule: factual, cost-first, never promotional.

effort_ladders.method: Values digitised from the published figure in Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 announcement — point positions read off the chart, so treat costs as ±~5% and scores as ±~0.5 points. The max-effort endpoints are exact: 43.3 / 33.7 / 18.7 are quoted numerically in the launch coverage and match the plotted points, which is what anchors the rest of the reading.
effort_ladders.harness: Internal run of Frontier-Bench v0.1 on the mini-SWE-agent harness with a GKE backend; mean reward over 5 attempts per task. Opus 4.8 served as fallback on safety-classifier refusals for Opus 5 and Fable 5.
effort_ladders.caveat: Anthropic's own benchmark, own harness, own run — and three of the four models plotted are its own. Read it for the SHAPE of each model's cost/quality curve (where extra spend stops buying accuracy), not as a settled cross-lab ranking. No third party has reproduced it.

series.label: GPT-5.6 Sol
series.level_note: OpenAI exposes its own reasoning-effort settings, not Anthropic's five names — these are the rungs as Anthropic plotted them, so the labels are positional rather than an exact setting-for-setting match.

effort_ladder_note: effort_ladders = published cost-vs-performance curves where a single model is run at several effort/reasoning settings, so you can see what extra spend actually buys. Each ladder carries its publisher, harness, method and confidence, and is shown with those attached — vendor-run benchmarks are directional, never a settled ranking. A ladder is only listed when the publisher has released the figure; nothing here is modelled or extrapolated from list prices.
